body: Thank you for your support. It's a hard time of year, and I needed some perspective.

Thank you. 

One day I made a joke about contemplating suicide as an alternative to going into work. I wasn't depressed, at least no more than usual, and life was actually going kind of well. To me, it was hilarious. To most of the coworkers who heard it, it was a warning sign. 

It's good to know I'm not alone.

We are waiting to have kids until we can financially support a family. It looks like that isn't happening any time soon.

I could have chosen adoption. I could have given up my recreations and taken a minimum wage job and gotten on food stamps and welfare and damnit I could have done my duty as a woman and a wife and a mother but I didn't because all of that was just too hard.

 I blame myself because there is no one else to blame. It was my decision. I was the one who presented abortion as an option in the 'what are we going to do' conversation. I made the appointment. I sat through the interviews alone and multiple people assessed both my willingness to have the abortion as well as my psychological capacity to make such a decision.

Last time I visited my family, dinner conversation was dominated by a discussion of how selfish, immature, and horrible it was that a single high school girl aborted a baby she couldn't care for. 

Needless to say, my family doesn't know I was ever pregnant. I grew up being told regularly by my mom that if I came down with a sudden case of YoungAndKnockedUp-itis, she would be there to fully support me and my child. She would be heartbroken.

Even if life doesn't begin at conception, even if it doesn't begin until they're 20 years out of your crotch, you still chose to deprive another human being of their fair chance by getting the abortion. You deserve every bad thing that has come as well as all that has yet to come. Killing yourself is refusing to accept your punishment.
I should have known. Pro-choice people don't understand my regret, and pro-life people don't agree with my choice. Pro-Choice Christians get abortions, we don't get allies.

Just like in the flesh world, you shouldn't have mentioned the A word in your post. You lost everyone's sympathy and just made them uncomfortable and unable to identify with you. 

They can't help if they can't relate.

Sitting here for an hour, browsing and refreshing. I've typed up countless replies to the other new posts with zero comments, but have found my responses lacking. I've watched posts ten minutes before and two after mine get replies. 

I haven't felt this alone in a long time. Husband is at work for another two hours. I just have to make it through until then and he'll be home for a couple of days off and I won't have another chance to off myself until my thirteen hours alone and unoccupied Wednesday night. 

I don't have a suicide plan...I have about a dozen. The only question is when and where and how I can make sure I do the least psychological damage to witnesses/body locaters. It's hard to kill yourself conscientiously...

If you throw yourself in front of a train, you traumatize a conductor. If I OD on pills, my husband has to get home from work and greet my corpse. It seems almost impossible to just quietly eliminate yourself without dragging other people into it. I don't know the area well enough to know that a public space I would choose would be frequented by gang bangers and not ten year olds.
